commonPitfalls.title: J: confusing the letter J with IPA j
commonPitfalls.body: Real example. The J in 'jump' is not IPA j (the y in yes), but dʒ. The glyphs look similar, so it's easy to mix them up.

commonPitfalls.title: R: /ɹ/ becomes a growly 'zombie sound'
commonPitfalls.body: Real example. Overdoing R can add growl/roughness. Keep the tongue tip off contact points, relax, and focus on shaping rather than forcing sound.

commonPitfalls.title: oo: uː shortens toward ʊ (book/look)
commonPitfalls.body: Real example. If uː in goose/too gets too short and lax, it drifts toward ʊ in book/look. Pay attention to both length and lip/tongue tension.

commonPitfalls.title: th: /θ/ and /ð/ become /s/ or /z/
commonPitfalls.body: Lightly place the tongue tip against the teeth and let air leak. /θ/ is voiceless (think), /ð/ is voiced (this). Many learners replace them with /s/ or /z/.

commonPitfalls.title: L/R: confusing /l/ and /ɹ/
commonPitfalls.body: /l/: tongue tip touches the alveolar ridge (light). /ɹ/: tongue tip does not touch; curl/shape forward (right). Don't lump both together as a single 'r-like' sound.

commonPitfalls.title: V/B: /v/ becomes /b/
commonPitfalls.body: /v/: friction with lower lip and upper teeth (very). /b/: lips close then release (berry). The presence of friction is the key difference.

commonPitfalls.title: F/H: /f/ becomes /h/
commonPitfalls.body: /f/: lip + teeth friction (fine). /h/: breath from the throat (high). The mouth shape is different.

commonPitfalls.title: iː/ɪ: long vs short vowel contrast disappears
commonPitfalls.body: Beat /iː/ is longer and tenser; bit /ɪ/ is shorter and laxer. Not only length, but also oral tension changes.

commonPitfalls.title: æ: /æ/ drifts toward /e/
commonPitfalls.body: In 'cat', /æ/ requires a wider opening than /e/ in 'bed'.

commonPitfalls.title: ə: pronouncing schwa too clearly
commonPitfalls.body: The first vowel in 'about' is /ə/: weak and short. In English, only stressed vowels are clearly articulated.

commonPitfalls.title: Stress: stress placement shifts
commonPitfalls.body: Since vowel length/clarity changes, stress often impacts intelligibility more than consonants. Decide the stressed syllable first.

commonPitfalls.title: t/d: missing the American flap /ɾ/
commonPitfalls.body: In words like water/ladder, t/d can sound like [ɾ]. It's useful to know as a perception phenomenon, not just pronunciation.

commonPitfalls.title: ng: saying /ŋ/ as /nɡ/
commonPitfalls.body: Word-final 'ng' in 'sing' is typically /ŋ/ (not n + g). Some words pronounce g (like tongue), so it's easy to mix.
